events.region: Coastal Waters from San Mateo Point to the Mexican Border and out to 10 nm; Waters from San Mateo point to the Mexican Border Extending 10 to 60 nm out including San Clemente Island
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Seas 5 to 9 ft and west winds 20 to 25 knots will lead
to choppy seas and dangerous boating conditions.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from San Mateo Point to the Mexican
Border and out to 10 nm and Waters from San Mateo Point to the
Mexican Border Extending 10 to 60 nm out including San
Clemente Island.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PST today.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strongest winds will occur before 10 AM
today. Seas and winds will begin to diminish this afternoon,
but seas may remain above 7 feet into early Sunday, especially
south of San Clemente Island.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 7 feet with sets 8 to 10 feet along west-facing beaches.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected, particularly along west-facing beaches where surf
will be highest.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 10 AM PST Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Adjusted high tides will be near 6.2- 6.5
feet around midday today, which will combine with high surf to
produce minor coastal flooding. Highest surf is expected to
occur late today into early Sunday. Surf begins to subside
Sunday afternoon but will remain elevated into Monday.

events.region: Northern Arctic Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to two
inches. Winds gusting as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard
conditions will be intermittently possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The lull in snow and wind will continue
through Saturday morning before snowfall chances increase Saturday
afternoon through Sunday morning. Winds will increase thereafter
and be strongest Saturday afternoon into Sunday with gusts as high
as 60 mph possible and blizzard conditions returning.
